nodes.statement: Let d_1(P) be the number of pairs of points in P whose distance is exactly 1.
nodes.span: Let ${d_1(P)}$ denote the number of unit distances determined by these points
nodes.status_reason: definition of the central quantity

nodes.statement: There exist point sets P of size n with d_1(P) bounded below by n^{1 + c / \log\log n}.
nodes.span: There exists point sets ${P}$ of arbitrarily large cardinality ${n}$ such that ${d_1(P) \gg n^{1 +c / \log\log n}}$
nodes.status_reason: derived later in the text via the Gaussian integers

nodes.statement: There exist point sets P of size n with d_1(P) bounded below by n^{1 + c}.
nodes.span: There exists point sets ${P}$ of arbitrarily large cardinality ${n}$ such that ${d_1(P) \gg n^{1 + c}}$
nodes.status_reason: relies on Golod-Shafarevich towers which the reader does not hold

nodes.statement: There exist point sets P of size n with d_1(P) bounded below by n^{1 + c / \log\log\log n}.
nodes.span: There exists point sets ${P}$ of arbitrarily large cardinality ${n}$ such that ${d_1(P) \gg n^{1 + c / \log\log\log n}}$
nodes.status_reason: derived in the text via quadratic extensions

nodes.statement: A point set with a given number of pairs at distance m can be rescaled to yield the same number of unit distances.
nodes.span: any construction of a point set ${P}$ with a given value of ${d_m(P)}$ can be rescaled to another point set
nodes.status_reason: basic geometric scaling

nodes.statement: The constructions use elements of a ring of algebraic integers B up to a certain height.
nodes.span: involve taking all the elements of a certain ring ${B}$ of algebraic integers up to some height
nodes.status_reason: general strategy stated by the author

nodes.statement: Assume m is the product of t primes of size roughly T, where T is proportional to t log t.
nodes.span: assume to all have comparable magnitude, thus ${p_i \asymp T}$ for some ${T}$
nodes.status_reason: parameter choice for the construction

nodes.statement: If m splits into Dt primes in B, conjugate pairs generate 2^{Dt/2} solutions to the distance equation.
nodes.span: By selecting one element from each pair and multiplying, this generates ${2^{Dt/2}}$ solutions to (3) in ${B}$
nodes.status_reason: follows from prime splitting and conjugation symmetry

nodes.statement: The number of points n in B of height O(m^{1/2}) is approximately T^{Dt/2}.
nodes.span: n \approx (m^{1/2})^D \approx T^{D t / 2}
nodes.status_reason: follows from the rank D of B and the height bound

nodes.statement: The number of distance-m pairs is heuristically bounded below by n^{1 + \log 2 / \log t}.
nodes.span: d_m(P) \gtrapprox n 2^{Dt/2} \approx n^{1 + \frac{\log 2}{\log T}} \approx n^{1 + \frac{\log 2}{\log t}}
nodes.status_reason: combines the number of solutions with the size of n

nodes.statement: Instead of exact distance, weaken the condition to a congruence modulo mB.
nodes.span: weaken the target equation (3) to a congruence equation
nodes.status_reason: methodological shift to avoid unique factorization issues

nodes.statement: Let m be the product of t primes congruent to 1 mod 4, with T proportional to t log t.
nodes.span: product ${m = p_1 \dots p_t}$ of ${t}$ (rational) primes of size ${\asymp T}$
nodes.status_reason: specific parameter choice for Theorem 3

nodes.statement: Let q_1 to q_g be g primes of size G, with G proportional to g log g.
nodes.span: distinct medium-sized (rational) primes ${q_1,\dots,q_g}$ of size ${\asymp G}$
nodes.status_reason: specific parameter choice for Theorem 3

nodes.statement: Work in the number field generated by i and the square roots of the g primes.
nodes.span: work in the number field \displaystyle {\bf Q}(i, \sqrt{q_1}, \dots, \sqrt{q_g})
nodes.status_reason: definition of the field for Theorem 3

nodes.statement: The covolume of the lattice B is bounded by G^{O(gD)}.
nodes.span: covolume of the lattice, which up to lower order terms is basically ${(\sqrt{q_1} \dots \sqrt{q_g})^D}$
nodes.status_reason: follows from the Walsh-Fourier transform embedding

nodes.statement: Any sublattice of B of index I contains a vector of height O(I^{1/D} G^{O(g)}).
nodes.span: any sublattice of ${B}$ of index ${I}$ will contain a vector of length ${O(I^{1/D} G^{O(g)})}$
nodes.status_reason: relies on a specific form of Minkowski's convex body theorem not held by the reader

nodes.statement: A sublattice of index m^{D/2} satisfying the congruence condition contains an element of height O(m^{1/2} G^{O(g)}).
nodes.span: contain a non-zero element ${w}$ of height ${O(m^{1/2} G^{O(g)})}$
nodes.status_reason: applies the Minkowski bound to the specific index

nodes.statement: There are at least 2^{tD/4} sublattices of index m^{D/2} that satisfy the congruence condition.
nodes.span: find at least ${2^{tD/4}}$ different sublattices ${\Lambda}$ of index ${m^{D/2}}$ that obey (9)
nodes.status_reason: derived via the Chinese remainder theorem and local structure

nodes.statement: The structure of B/pB allows generating 2^{D/4} subspaces per prime that satisfy the condition.
nodes.span: generate either ${2^{D/2}}$ or ${2^{D/4}}$ different subspaces ${V}$ of dimension ${D/2}$
nodes.status_reason: follows from the isomorphism of B/pB to products of finite fields

nodes.statement: Pigeonholing yields at least 2^{tD/4} / O(G)^{O(gD)} solutions to the exact distance equation.
nodes.span: by pigeonholing one can now also get at least at least ${2^{tD/4} / O(G)^{O(gD)}}$ solutions
nodes.status_reason: pigeonholes the congruence solutions into exact solutions

nodes.statement: Choosing g proportional to t / log t recovers the bound in Theorem 3.
nodes.span: choose ${g}$ to be a small multiple of ${t / \log t}$ , then we soon calculate that ${\log t \asymp \log\log\log n}$
nodes.status_reason: optimizes parameters to yield the final asymptotic
